abstract: Posterior staphyloma is a hallmark of pathologic myopia, but the cellular and molecular changes of the overlying retina remain poorly understood. We combined the histopathology of human eyes with posterior staphyloma with label-free proteomics of vitreous from non-myopic eyes (n = 4) and highly myopic eyes without (n = 3) or with posterior staphyloma (n = 7) and measured soluble vitreous iron in an independent series of 31 eyes. In the staphyloma, the retina collapsed at the transition zones into a vimentin- and GFAP-positive glial scar containing Iba1-positive microglia, with iron deposits, increased ferritin and disorganized scleral collagen. The vitreous proteome was not globally altered, but protein modules defined a priori to mirror these lesions revealed an activation of the classical complement pathway and an increased ferritin-to-transferrin ratio, both specific to staphylomatous eyes, whereas neuron- and photoreceptor-derived proteins were already decreased in highly myopic eyes without staphyloma. Soluble vitreous iron was lower in staphylomatous eyes than in non-myopic eyes and in highly myopic eyes without staphyloma, independently of total protein content. These findings suggest that complement activation and iron sequestration characterize the retinal degeneration associated with posterior staphyloma, and that the vitreous provides a window on these processes.
